newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen up on banking sector worries.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen up on banking sector worries.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract was higher in early Tokyo trade on Wednesday.
Traders said the December was up on market talk, later denied, that Nippon Credit Bank might hold an emergency news briefing.
A Nippon Credit Bank official told Reuters that the bank has no plan to hold such a briefing but was preparing to issue a comment on its falling share price. He did not elaborate.
The December stood at 99.23 as of 0136 GMT, up from the previous day's 99.21.

A city bank trader said a fall in Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) shares in the morning triggered the rumours, leading to speculation that the Bank of Japan will have to maintain its low interest rate policy, and led to buying of the December.
NCB shares dropped to their lowest level for the current fiscal year on Wednesday. The shares were down 26 yen at 190 as of 0140 GMT.
NCB's denial of plans to hold a briefing has had little effect on Euroyen futures so far, a city bank trader said.
Traders said the market feels that there will still be liquidity problems at some banks and that the BOJ has no choice but to maintain easy credit.
Worries about the financial sector are seen as buying incentives for Euroyen futures as they support the market's view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would need to maintain a low interest rate policy.
"The December hit 99.25 as it broke resistance at 99.22. Buying was largely short-covering," said a city bank trader.
Market participants are becoming more bullish after the December's rise to 99.25, but they are still cautious ahead of the weekend G7 meeting, traders said.
"If yen/dollar stabilises after the G7, that would be welcomed by the market," said the trader.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.50 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
The BOJ injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market on Wednesday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.

About 170 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.54 percent, up from 0.53 percent on Tuesday. Three-month CDs were last issued at 0.54 percent on August 30, 1996.

CD rates are facing upward pressure as a massive amount of CDs are due to mature before the current fiscal year ends on March 31, traders said. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780 --Tokyo Treasury Desk, +81-3-5473-3748
